newsitem.title: CANADA: Clearnet starts wireless business network.
newsitem.headline: Clearnet starts wireless business network.

text.p: Clearnet Communications Inc said on Friday that it will launch on Monday its new wireless business communications service under the trade name MiKE.

MiKE is a digital wireless communications service for business that integrates mobile phone, dispatch or group and private call radio, alphanumeric paging and messaging services into a single handset.

Through a Motorola Inc handset, subscribers will be able to communicate via cellular phone and two-way radio, and receive text messages, including those via the Internet, and pager messages, company officials told reporters.
The network will initially be operational in the corridor between Quebec City and Windsor, Ontario, but the company said it planned eventually to roll out the service nationally.
"We want to be anywhere with MiKE that business takes place," said Wade Oosterman, vice president of sales and marketing.

Clearnet's cellular telephone tariff would match those of Canada's two largest cellular phone service providers, BCE Mobile Communications Inc unit Bell Mobility and Rogers Cantel Communications Inc, he said.

Clearnet officials declined to discuss the potential or expected subscriber base and revenues for MiKE. Oosterman said the company has raised C$1.1 billion of financing to fund the expansion of the MiKE network and a personal communications services (PCS) network that it plans to launch nationally in Canada in mid-1997.
But MiKE will offer local calling areas that are on average 15 to 20 percent larger and calls will be billed by the second instead of by the minute.
The great advantage for subscribers will be the flexibility offered by providing all four communications services in one handset, and the quality of a digital network, Oosterman said.

A similar combination phone service was launched on September 16 in certain areas of the United States by Nextel Communications Inc, a 20 percent shareholder in Clearnet. The Nextel system also uses Motorola technology. -- Reuters Montreal bureau (514) 985-2434
